... The Almighty's saying: "And He is with you wherever you are" (57:4), following the mention of the heavens and the earth, contains an allusion, as if the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to tell us that the heavens and the earth are an obedient creation that performs its task and does not deviate from what it was created for; therefore it is not held to account. As for you, you are held to account because you are free to choose.

"And He is with you wherever you are": meaning, no outward thing veils Him from the inward, and no inward thing veils Him from the outward.

"And Allah is Seer of what you do": so He, glorified is He, is with you and sees you. Had it been a companionship of essence, He would not have said "and Allah is Seer of what you do." Rather, it is a companionship of sight. He mentioned sight, which is seeing, and such matters cannot be imagined; rather, take it in its utmost perfection, which belongs to Him, glorified is He.

As long as we are in the companionship of Allah and under His sight, let us observe that and act accordingly, and let us take account of Him. Why not, when we take account of the companionship and gaze of people...

We always say concerning Him, exalted is He: "With the Essence there is no 'where'" (laysa ma'a al-'ayn ayn). Every atom in His dominion, exalted is He, is under His sight and nothing is hidden from Him...

He it is who sends down to His servant clear signs, that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And indeed Allah is to you Kind and Merciful.

That is, to His Prophet (ﷺ) are clear signs, [al-Hadid] evident in their indication of the Creator, glory be to Him. The signs are either cosmic, such as the sun, the moon, the night and the day, or they are miracles and wonders that accompany the sending of the messengers, in order to establish for people the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah. Then there are the signs of the Wise Reminder, the verses of the Qur'an, which carry the method and the rulings that organise the movement of life in a way that brings people to the blessed goal.

So these are three forms of signs, and each has its aim and purpose, and Allah, glory be to Him, summed them up in His saying: ﴿that He may bring you out from darkness into light﴾ [al-Hadid]. Light and darkness are opposites. We know light as that effect by which we see things, so it has a known existence; as for darkness, it has no existence in itself, but is rather a negation in the absence of light.

We have said: light is what makes us see things, so we walk by guidance and do not collide with anything, whereas in darkness one stumbles, the weak are crushed and the strong crush us. This concerns sensory light. Likewise is moral light, which is the light of the method and the values by which we are guided on the paths of life:

﴿There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book. By it Allah guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path﴾ [al-Ma'idah]. So it is light upon light.

And He spoke of the disbelievers who turned their backs on the method of Allah and opposed it: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire, and when it lit up what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing﴾.

Thus what is meant here is the immaterial: ﴿that He may bring you out from the darknesses of disbelief into the light of faith﴾. And ﴿indeed Allah is to you Kind and Merciful﴾. Ra'fah (kindness) is to remove pain and misery from a person and draw out his ailment, and rahmah (mercy) is to protect him afterwards from being struck by pain or ailment.

Similarly His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra']. So the Qur'an, the method of Allah, contains healing for the diseases of society: it awakens them from heedlessness, turns them away from the paths of corruption, and sets right whatever defect or flaw is in them. Then mercy comes as a safeguard for them against slipping, and protects them, so these ailments do not strike them again.

We have given the example of the method of the Truth [by the evidence of usage]: if we walk upon it, no defect will ever befall us, for the maker of a thing knows best what sets it right, and is most eager for its soundness.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 57, verse 13:

"The Day" means the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the Day when you see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right hands,﴾ which brings them to Paradise. ﴿On that same Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who believed: "Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light."﴾ [Al-Hadid] That is, "Wait for us, that we may take a portion of your light, by which we may be illuminated and guided." ﴿It will be said to them: "Go back behind you and seek light."﴾

That is: go back to the world and seek the light that guides you now, because the light by which we are guided now is what we sent ahead as righteous deeds in the world, on the day we believed in Allah and His Messenger and obeyed. Now we reap the fruit of what we sent ahead, and you must begin a new life, where there is obligation and work, for today is recompense, not action.

Reflect here on the greatness of the Qur'anic expression. The dialogue takes place between the believers and the hypocrites, yet the verb is built in the passive, ﴿qīla﴾ (قيل, "it was said"), and it does not say "the believers said to the hypocrites," so that there is no gloating in the scene, and so that the believers are not made to stand in that position. It is as though the voice came to them from a direction they do not recognise.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So a wall with a gate was struck between them.﴾ Between the believers and the hypocrites, with a wall that has a gate. Thus Allah, glorified is He, ends this dialogue and separates the believers from the hypocrites with a wall that has a gate, so that they neither see them nor hear them, because the believer by nature is tender of heart.

So their Lord, mighty and majestic, protects their hearing and protects their sight from being distressed by what the hypocrites suffer in Hell, Allah forbid, by a wall ﴿with a gate, its inner side containing mercy, and its outer side facing the torment﴾: on the side of the believers is mercy, and on the side of the hypocrites is the torment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 57, verse 15:

This is a cutting off of their hopes for deliverance: the destiny awaiting them is inescapable, with no way out and no escape. Even ransom will not be accepted from them if one of them wishes to ransom himself from the punishment of God. Someone may suppose that this ruling is specific to the hypocrites who were previously discussed, because God has informed of them that they are in the lowest level of the Fire (al-dark al-asfal), and ﴿you will not find for them any helper﴾ [An-Nisa 4:145].

So God, glorified and exalted, makes clear that this ruling also includes their likes among the disbelievers: ﴿nor from those who disbelieved﴾. This is because the disbelievers are less guilty than the hypocrites. So He said: ﴿ransom will not be accepted from those, nor from these,﴾ and they must face this destiny.

﴿Your abode is the Fire﴾: your place of return and your final dwelling. ﴿It is your mawla (protector)﴾: that is, the Fire is your mawla, because a person in this situation needs a wali (guardian) to whom he is loyal and a nasir (helper) who supports him. Whoever does not have God as his wali and nasir on this day, then the Fire, may God protect us, is his wali.

Therefore He said in the verse of an-Nisa: ﴿and you will not find for them a helper﴾ [An-Nisa 4:145], and He said: ﴿they have no wali nor nasir﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:8]. Whoever has the Fire as his wali and nasir, then wretched is the protector and wretched is the helper, and wretched is the place of return and the destination.

Are you not noticing the connection here between the hardness and petrification of hearts and the revival of the earth after its death? It is as if the Exalted and Glorified God wants to say to us: if your hearts have died and hardened, and if the teachings of the religion have been lost to you, then do not despair, for the One who revives the earth after its death is able to revive the dead hearts.

So: it was good news for them that they would return to the arena of faith in a better state than they had been in. "We have already made the signs clear to you, so that you may use your reason." Among the signs is that God revives hearts through remembrance and the verses, just as He revives the earth through rain. Each of them is a sign that requires from us reflection, understanding, and contemplation.

This verse exposes the world and unveils its falseness. Some people work in this world as though it were an end in itself, but it is not so. Here the Almighty describes it with several attributes in the form of restriction (qasr), meaning: it is nothing other than these.

Play (la'b) and diversion (lahw) and adornment (zinah). Play (la'b) is a movement of a person that has no good purpose, like the play of children at home when they play and break things. This play is merely amusement for them, a way of filling time and expending energy. Play happens before the age of legal responsibility (taklif); if it happens after taklif, it is diversion (lahw), because it distracts you from righteous deeds.

... "Hasten (sabiqu) towards forgiveness..." It is as if forgiveness is the goal and the aim, just as you say, "I travelled from Cairo to Alexandria." This goal is not attained except through competition and earnest, persistent striving; forgiveness is not attained through negligence and laziness. The competition here is a competition in righteous deeds and acts of obedience, a competition in submitting to the commands of God.

In another place He, glorified is He, said: "And hasten (wa sari'u) towards forgiveness from your Lord..." [Al 'Imran: 133]. Hastening and competing signify reciprocal striving, sharing and rivalry among the believers who submit to the method of God, each one wanting to outstrip and to rise towards the sought-after goal that is common to them all, which is forgiveness, "towards forgiveness from your Lord..."

But in another verse, He said concerning our master Zakariyya and our master Yahya: "Indeed they used to hasten (yusari'una) in the good deeds..." [al-Anbiya': 90]. He did not say "towards the good deeds," because good deeds are a means and not an end in themselves; good deeds are a means to the supreme goal, which is forgiveness.

He said "al-khayrat" (the good deeds) in the plural form, because it is a wide field that accommodates the aspiration of faith. Every believer takes from it according to his eagerness and hastens in it according to his effort and capability. The performance of good thus varies: the more deeply you go into it and the more you hasten, the more rank you take from it in proportion to it...

The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, clarifies this meaning for us in his saying: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom God has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in what is right, and a man whom God has given knowledge and he judges by it among the people."

Envy here means ghibta (admiring emulation) and noble rivalry. The origin of rivalry (munafasa) is the length of breath. Therefore our master 'Umar said to our master al-'Abbas: "Come, let us compete," meaning: let us dive into the water and see which of us has the longer breath? It is well known that the more healthy a person's lungs are, able to hold the largest amount of air, the longer his breath and his staying under water will be.

So: let us race in the good deeds to see which of us is foremost, which of us reaches his goal first...

And His saying, exalted is He: "...and a Garden whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth." The Garden is mentioned after forgiveness, for God forgives them their sins first and then admits them into the Garden... Forgiveness either is preceded by a sin which forgiveness erases, or forgiveness is by concealing the sin from you so that it never reaches you at all.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, gives us an example and clarification of the Garden, because it is unseen and unknown to us, so He brings it near to the minds with something known and witnessed. We see the heaven and the earth and their expanse in length and breadth.

So in describing the Garden He said: "a Garden whose breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth..." He mentioned the breadth and did not mention the length, and it is well known that breadth is always less than length. So if its breadth, that is, the Garden's, is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth in its expanse, then what of its length? This is a metaphor for vastness.

And His saying, exalted is He: "It has been prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers..." That is: it has already been prepared and readied to receive those who believe in God and His messenger. It is a settled matter and not something still in the process of being created...

...Almighty God says: "We indeed sent Our messengers with clear proofs" — that is, the manifest signs that draw people's attention to the existence of the Truth, glorified is He, and that confirm the messengers whom God sent to guide creation.

The signs are either cosmic (kawniyyah), or miracles that confirm the messengers, or the verses of the Wise Book, which carry the method and carry the rulings from God for creation. "And We sent down with them the Book" — that is, the books that were sent down from God. The Book (kitab) is that which is written.

"And the Balance (mizan)" — that is, the balance of Truth that weighs things, determines them and makes them clear. The balance is not restricted to material things that have density only; rather it is a balance that weighs everything, material and immaterial, with truth. Concerning material things He says: "And give full measure and weight with justice" (6:152), and He commanded the establishment of this balance in everything.

"And when you judge between people, to judge with justice" (4:58). Even in courts you find them taking the balance as a symbol of justice and raising it as their emblem, and the balance has two equal pans to indicate a just judgment.

The balance that the messengers brought is the balance that distinguishes between truth and falsehood. So long as there are messengers, clear signs, and a method that benefits people and organises their lives, the movement of life must be upright.

Therefore Hudhayfah said: "There was a time when I did not mind which of you I pledged allegiance to: if he was a Muslim, his religion would return him to me, and if he was a Jew or a Christian, his administrator (saay) would return him to me." The saa'i is the one who observes and follows the movements of people. "But today, I would not pledge allegiance except to so-and-so and so-and-so."

So: affairs are not upright except under the shade of this method, and there is no happiness for creation except by it. If this method is obliterated, disorder must occur in the balance, so truth becomes falsehood and falsehood becomes truth...

So: the Messenger of God returned the balance to the religion and the Sharia, and to the Book and the clear proofs. Whoever adheres to the Book and the clear proofs does not have truth and falsehood; rather, it is one clear truth with nothing else. If people differ concerning the clear proofs, falsehood must arise, and then the balance comes to distinguish between truth and falsehood.

Therefore God said after it: "And We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice" — that is, equity. The Book is for legislation and the execution of rulings, and the Balance is for heedlessness if it occurs, or for transgression, so it makes clear truth and falsehood.

As long as people uphold justice and equity, the whole world is at rest: either justice springing from the conscience of individuals, or justice from the judiciary that judges between them...

So: We sent down the Book for the one who adheres to it, and the Balance... which distinguishes truth from falsehood for the one who does not adhere, "that people may uphold" — all of them — "justice." So when the murderer is subjected to retaliation and the thief's hand is cut off, no one dares to kill or to steal. He did not say "that the believers may uphold justice," but rather "the people," all people.

"And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people" — that is, just as We sent down the Book and sent down the Balance, We likewise sent down iron. Iron, although its place is the earth, its origin is from above, and iron is a sign of strength: whoever is not restrained by the Qur'an is restrained by iron... Thus God, exalted is He, says to His Prophet, peace be upon him: just as We gave you the Qur'an, We gave you iron and the sword, so do with it what you will, and confront with it the disbelievers and the rebels who are not restrained by the Book...

His saying, "wherein is mighty violence" (fihi ba's shadid), indicates that iron is the strongest equipment in life, and reality confirms this...

Then there is another function of iron: "and that God may know who helps Him and His messengers in the unseen" — here is an allusion to the sword by which victory is achieved, for the sword is for one who does not find with him the Book and the clear proofs.

His saying: "that God may know who helps Him and His messengers in the unseen" — that is, the knowledge of what occurs in reality; otherwise God, exalted is He, knows everything from eternity, and nothing is hidden from Him. So the intended meaning is not knowledge of decree but knowledge of actual occurrence.

He said, "who helps Him and His messengers," because helping God is helping His messengers, and helping God's messengers is helping God. Therefore He said: "And obey God and obey the Messenger" (5:92), and He said: "Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God" (4:80), because there is an interpenetration of rulings here...

His saying "in the unseen" (bil-ghayb) — with faith in the unseen and the sight of the sword. This one defends an unseen cause, which is the Resurrection; and God, whom you do not see, defends an unseen cause, but when He gives life to the mind through the Book or the sword...

Therefore, when the disbelievers persisted in their disbelief, God said to His Messenger: "So turn away from one who turns away from Our remembrance" (53:29). The hamza in "a'ridh" is the hamza of removal, meaning: leave them and turn away from calling them with the signs and clear proofs.

The meaning of God's help, as He, glorified is He, said: "If you help God, He will help you" (47:7) — that is, if you help God with your strength, He will help you with His strength. So your only duty is to direct: "And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw" (8:17).

God is capable of destroying these disbelievers in the twinkling of an eye, so why war? It is said: if God had destroyed them by a hidden command without the intervention of the Muslims in war, they would have said it was a cosmic sign. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: "Fight them; God will punish them by your hands" (9:14) — by your hands, so the matter is more painful.

The verse concludes with His saying, glorified is He: "Indeed, God is Strong, Mighty," affirming that God is the possessor of strength and the possessor of might, lest we understand from His saying "that God may know who helps Him and His messengers in the unseen" that God needs help from His creation.

God is the One of strength, the Victorious, the Mighty who cannot be overcome. He said to you, "help Me," so that your hands would be in the hand of the Imam, and the victory through you would be an elevation for you; and when the enemies are subdued, they are subdued by you and humbled before you.

...then He describes his followers: "And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion (ra'fa) and mercy (rahma)." Ra'fa is that which removes pain and hardship, and rahma is to give with increase and kindness.

"And monasticism (rahbaniyya) which they invented..." Rahbaniyya is excessive devotion in worship. The followers of Jesus went to extremes in worship: they withdrew into monasteries (sawami') and deprived themselves of women. Monasticism is mentioned in a book they wrote in 1935; this book spoke about Wadi al-Natrun, and its title is: Wadi al-Natrun and its Monks. They also said: monasticism came into being one hundred and fifty years after Jesus...
